catalog_quote: 2.1 syllable structure As in other Mixtec languages, the basic structure of the word in NM is two syllables called a couplet. ... 3. STRESS Phrase stress is on the last syllable of the phrase. Word stress is on the first syllable of the couplet. Therefore a couplet at the end of a phrase has stress on both the first and second syllables because it has both word and phrase stress, such as in the word ˈnu⁴ˈniʔ³ <corn> in the first example below. Likewise a couplet spoken in isolation is stressed on both syllables as it is itself a phrase, as in the last example. Also single syllable words and clitics are stressed; as is the first person singular pronouns clitic =niʔ⁴ in the first example
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress falls on the first syllable of the couplet (the bimoraic CV.CV root that is the basic word shape in Mixtec), i.e. word-initial/root-initial. Separately, phrase stress falls on the last syllable of the phrase, so a couplet that ends a phrase, or is spoken in isolation (citation form), carries stress on both syllables. Monosyllabic words and clitics are also stressed.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not discussed as such; the second syllable of a phrase-final or isolated couplet receives phrase stress in addition to the word-initial word stress.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated for word stress. Note the transcriptions in the PDF text are garbled by font substitution (e.g. 'AnuKAniCB DcornE' = [nuni] with stress mark and tone digits, quotes rendered as D..E); the prose is clean. The ms. is a draft 'posted as is without peer review'. Elsewhere it notes that in unstressed syllables [ɓ]/[ñ] have optional variants.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level stress vs phrase-level stress explicitly distinguished; citation forms (words in isolation) show both, i.e. stress on both syllables of the couplet. Data from Santiago Nuyoo speakers (dialect nuyo1238).
new_statements.identity_note: The statement comes from a description of the Santiago Nuyoo variety (Glottolog dialect nuyo1238, one of the two dialects of sout3000 [meh]); Harris & Harris 2018 (p. 2, fn. 1) say the Santa María Yucuhiti variety (yucu1249) is 'muy similar' and shares the ISO code. Harris & Harris 2006 call the language 'Nuyoo Mixtec (NM)' / 'Phonology of Santiago Nuyoo Mixtec'; SIL's archive title is 'Nuyoo Mixtec Phonology' with subject language Southwestern Tlaxiaco Mixtec [meh].

tone_statements.citation: Auderset, Sandra. 2022. Supplementary Material: Standardization of tone notations. 'Rates of change and phylogenetic signal in Mixtec tone' (supplement to Language Dynamics and Change 14(1): 1-41, 2024). 25 pp. Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology / UC Santa Barbara, dated August 15, 2022; distributed as definitions/ in the Mixtec Sound Change Database 2.0 (MixteCaSo), GitHub SAuderset/MixteCaSo, archived Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.10143870 (v2.0.0 = 10.5281/zenodo.14980449, 2025-03-06).
tone_statements.quote: Santa María Yucuhiti Mixtec The data for this variety is from Josserand (1983). Tones are marked with diacritics throughout (MULG). This variety has three level tones (high, mid, and low) but not all combinations are attested. ... This results in 7 contrastive tone melodies. The final glottal stop has no effect on tone realization. ... Santiago Nuyoo Mixtec The data for this variety is from Josserand (1983). ... There is relatively little data. There are three level tones (low, mid, high) which combine freely. There is one entry with a falling contour on the second mora, resulting in 10 contrastive tone melodies. Generally, *H has a mid tone reflex and *L a low tone. There is a merger of the *HL set with the other high tone sets.
tone_statements.locator: p. 8, section 'Group 6', entries 'Santa María Yucuhiti Mixtec' and 'Santiago Nuyoo Mixtec'; Table 13 (p. 8) and Table 14 (p. 9) list the melodies in Chao numbers (1.1 1.3 1.5 3.1 3.3 3.5 5.5 for Yucuhiti; all nine level combinations plus 5.51 for Nuyoo)
tone_statements.summary: Three level tones L M H (Chao 1/3/5) per mora of the bimoraic couplet, from Josserand 1983 transcriptions: Nuyoo 9 level melodies + one contour melody 5.51 (10 total); Yucuhiti 7 melodies (H on first mora only before H); Proto-Mixtec *H reflected as mid, *L as low; final glottal stop does not affect tone (Yucuhiti); no downstep, floating tones or stress discussed for these varieties.

sources.citation: Auderset, Sandra. 2024. Rates of change and phylogenetic signal in Mixtec tone. Language Dynamics and Change 14(1): 1-41. Leiden: Brill. (published online 2024-06-13)
sources.note: Comparative study of tone change in 42 Mixtec varieties incl. Santiago Nuyoo (Josserand 1983 data): Mixtec TBU is the mora; Nuyoo has mid reflex of Proto-Mixtec *high, low of *low; no inventory given.

tone.quote: The tone-bearing unit (TBU) in Mixtec is the mora, which means that each ‘couplet’ has two tones. These two tones can be level or contour tones, depending on the variety. … I established tone correspondences across the 42 languages of the sample. … All varieties except Peñoles, Coatzospam, Tepango, and Jicaltepec have a mid tone reflex for Proto-Mixtec *high, while the five mentioned varieties have a low tone reflex.
